contract: Durable ingest of one pinned state/artifact version of a tenant's document over a consumer-owned Ecto Repo on PostgreSQL 16: an ingest record, its batches, counted embedding attempts and staged chunks in four Piece-owned tables that Migration.install/1 creates under the state/tenant-isolation floor. submit/3 inserts the ingest (identity tenant, source_ref, version; equal canonical request returns it, another is conflict) and its prepare job in one transaction and re-enqueues a stranded one; bounded integration/jobs steps, each acting only in its own state under the ingest row lock and each killed at its fixed deadline: prepare (artifact get, document-parse, text-chunking with chunk_size 2,000..8,192 and overlap 0..200, chunk and request bounds, NUL under text_search, greedy batches by the ai-embedding canonical request), embed (one batch at a time; each attempt recorded pending before admission, dispatched through delivery/effect-intent under the step's own Task.Supervisor, classified by status when recovered; throttled, overloaded, credentials_unavailable, not_dispatched and completed_lost get new counted attempts up to max_attempts 1..5, an unknown outcome fails until resubmit/3) and index (search-data put_source/5 with if_newer and the parsed text's SHA-256; indexed or superseded with the staged-chunk delete in one transaction). status/3, paged attempts/3 with usage for the host's metering, cancel/3, resubmit/3 and verify/1; fixed error atoms, READ COMMITTED writes, no exactly-once Effect, no RunEngine Run.
limits: Scripted providers only: no claim about embedding, retrieval or ranking quality, and no live provider.

No exactly-once Effect: a completed_lost attempt is a second paid call, a throttle or overload may have been processed and an unknown attempt may have been charged; the attempts record keeps that visible but cannot prevent it.

With a durable Store each admitted attempt leaves one intent whose arguments are the batch's chunk texts, outside the tenant floor; the Piece removes none, and neither cancel/3 nor delete_source/4 removes them. Under a Memory Store an intent lasts only until a restart, and an interrupted attempt whose intent is not found is unknown even when it was never sent.
Oban job rows carry the tenant and the ingest ID, outside the floor.

Step timings are observations on this host, not guarantees: a slower host can fail a large document {:step_failed, :prepare}; a version too large to write within statement_timeout_ms + 2,000 ms ends {:step_failed, :index}, and a cancel of it can leave the version stored.
new/1 checks the request's model and dimension against the index descriptor, not its provider, so a provider mismatch is found only at the index step, after the paid calls.

Oban's job timeout is not used; the bound is the step's own deadline, and the Lifeline Need (rescue_after over the largest step deadline plus 60 s) is the host's. A rescue of a live embed job, which the Need excludes, can classify its in-flight attempt as unknown or not_dispatched. A rescue_after below the Lifeline Need, or a host that runs the worker outside Oban, can leave two live runs of one index job key: the second can fail the ingest while the first still writes, so a version can be stored for the first time after its ingest was cancelled. A cancel of an ingest that failed at index can also leave the version that its index step wrote stored.

indexed is not live state: a later delete_source/4 or higher version leaves it indexed; a delete that lands while a crashed index run awaits its re-run ends the ingest superseded although its first write committed.

A stranded ingest waits for an equal submit/3; there is no sweeper. An older version is embedded in full before its index step finds it stale. Batches run one at a time. The index step holds every chunk and vector of the version in memory.
A failed ingest keeps its staged chunks until it is cancelled; ingest and attempt records are never pruned; deleted rows stay in dead tuples, WAL and backups until PostgreSQL reclaims them.

One config serves one queue and one search index. The actor and the caller are host-vouched, not authenticated. The parsed text is untrusted content that the Piece does not mark; ingesting grants no authority and prevents no injection.
log: false silences only the Logger: the consumer Repo's Ecto query telemetry still receives every query's parameters, including the tenant, source reference, chunk content and encoded vectors.

Two databases that share one effect-intent Store and one embedding binding must not also reuse the same schema prefix and index identity: their equal submissions get one ingest ID and so one intent per attempt.
The state/tenant-isolation limits apply: the table owner can turn forcing off or drop the policies, and a superuser or BYPASSRLS role ignores them.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios of groups 1-3 on the worker's own PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector, a real Oban 2.24.2 instance drained in the test, a scripted provider that counts its calls and a real state/artifact store over the disposable MinIO, the intent Store on integration/sql except the Memory cases: 1 each bad field of new/1 and of every call is invalid before any query (counted on the Repo's telemetry), the 64/65-byte tenant, U+0085 actor, :head, chunk_size 1,999/2,000/8,192/8,193, overlap 200/201, max_input_bytes 7,999/8,000, model and dimension against the descriptor; equal, other-actor, conflicting and versioned submits; two equal submits behind a barrier store one ingest and one job; an injected enqueue failure, a caller transaction and REPEATABLE READ write nothing; index_mismatch; 2 HTML and Markdown staged chunks equal TextChunking.chunk/4 of the parsed text with text_sha256 and parser; artifact integrity mismatch, deleted and access denied; store_unavailable retried and failing on the last attempt; parse, chunk, combining-mark and escaped-quote oversize and NUL failures with no provider call; hand-counted greedy batches (32 ASCII, 10 three-byte, 8 four-byte, 16 newline chunks per call, max_inputs 4); two prepare runs (sequential and behind a barrier) leave one set of staged chunks and one batch-0 job; a prepare run held at its commit while another run fails the ingest and resubmit/3 makes a new job current writes nothing; a committed-then-erroring last attempt writes nothing; 1 MiB of four-byte emoji prepares within the real 120,000 ms deadline (observation printed); 3 vectors reach put_source element for element; retry_after 7, overload 5 s and 5 × 2^(n-1) backoff by attempt number, also after resubmit/3; exhaustion at max_attempts 1 and 5; credentials_unavailable, authentication_failed; unknown and a hanging provider with one call and the call dead before the job returns; resubmit after unknown and exhausted with continued numbers and no re-embedding of completed batches; completed_lost re-embedding with a new ref and exhaustion on the last attempt; a crash after pending gives not_dispatched with no intent in the Store, and under an emptied Memory Store unknown with no call; a deadline kill takes the send down and the next run records unknown, never two live calls; task_start after the dispatched barrier is unknown; two runs holding one completed outcome record one and enqueue one next or index job; a stale embed job erroring on its last attempt writes nothing; attempts/3 pages at limit 1, 2 and 256. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

Listed scenarios of groups 4, 5, 7 and 9 on the same stack: an indexed ingest's query/2 candidates carry source_digest equal to text_sha256; an index job run again after indexed and a host delete makes no put_source call; a crash after the committed write and a re-run end indexed with no staged chunk; index steps of versions 1 and 2 at once in both commit orders keep version 2 (version 1 indexed or superseded); version 1 after version 2 is superseded; delete_source/4 during embedding, between the write and the indexed transaction, and after a crash there give superseded, indexed and superseded with the source deleted; non-unit vectors fail {:index, :incompatible_embedding}; an injected indeterminate is retried; cancel in requested, preparing, embedding and failed, a late outcome recorded with no vector, indexing, terminal and not_failed results; a deadline passed on attempts 1-2 retried and on all three step_failed; raising prepare, embed and index steps fail step_failed and resubmit restarts the step; a killed step process is retried; a stranded ingest is re-enqueued by an equal submit and a live one is not; a replaced embed job retried by Oban.retry_job/2 while its successor is snoozed writes nothing and makes no provider call; the deadline, job attempt and backoff values; status at each state. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

Group 6: the whole Oban instance killed with reason :kill and a 50 ms shutdown grace while the step is held at its seam (job row left executing) during prepare, between two batches and after the index write; a new instance on the same Repo with Lifeline rescue_after 200 ms rescues the job and the ingest ends indexed with one version stored and no staged chunk; the same kill during an in-flight provider call leaves the intent Dispatched in the integration/sql Store and the ingest ends embedding_unknown with one call; a fresh VM that has loaded no dependency module decodes the stored reason, parser, outcome, usage and staged vector and the closed version 1 reason and outcome set. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

Group 8 as the ELZ-285 application role (ELZOO_TEST_APP_ROLE; fails, not skips, without it or when it is superuser or BYPASSRLS) with only the README grants, the Piece and its Oban instance on that role: verify/1 passes; without a tenant filter a T1 scope sees no T2 ingest, batch, attempt or staged chunk; a direct T2 insert fails 42501; status/3, cancel/3 and resubmit/3 of T2's ingest from T1 are not_found; verify/1 reports floor_missing after the floor of one table is dropped. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

Negative controls (temporary edits, reverted, never committed): writing without if_newer fails the version race where version 2 commits first; dropping prepare's commit guard (the job key and the preparing check) makes the second barrier run a job error on the staged-chunk constraint; dropping only its preparing check lets a run cancelled before its commit stage chunks into the cancelled ingest; dropping only its job-key check lets a run held at its commit, while another run fails the ingest and resubmit/3 makes a new job current, commit as a non-current job; dropping the own-state check of the last-attempt failure write ends the committed-then-error ingest failed; retrying an unknown outcome makes a second provider call; a staged-chunk delete in its own transaction after the indexed write with the crash seam between leaves staged chunks; dropping the indexed check of the index step makes a put_source call; an ownership check without the job key's enqueue number lets a replaced embed job make a second provider call; decoding without loading the defining modules first fails the fresh-VM read.

Oban 2.24.2 unique insert per (queue, job_key) with period :infinity and states :all, snooze with attempt - 1 in the Basic engine (no attempt consumed), backoff on {:error, _} and {:cancel, _} on the last attempt, the default :infinity job timeout (enforced only by :timer.exit_after/2, which an exit-trapping worker receives as a message), Lifeline rescue of executing jobs older than rescue_after (to available, or discarded when attempts are exhausted; it can re-run a live job) and drain_queue/2 are upstream contracts.

Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo.transact/2, in_transaction?/0, Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query!/4 with log: false and migration execute/1 are upstream behavior; a dying connection owner rolls its transaction back (DBConnection).

PostgreSQL 16 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row locks, READ COMMITTED statement snapshots after a lock wait, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waiting for a concurrent insert, primary-key uniqueness, row-level security with 42501 and table privileges are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex 0.22.4.
Elixir String.valid?/1, Regex, Task.Supervisor and :erlang.term_to_binary/2 with :deterministic and binary_to_term/2 with :safe for stored outcomes are upstream contracts.

OTP 29.1.2 links, monitors, exit trapping and Process.exit/2 with :kill (the deadline kill), supervisor shutdown of linked children and crypto:hash(sha256) for the ingest ID and request digest are upstream contracts.

The host runs the migration as the table owner, connects the application as a non-owner, non-bypass role with the README grants and READ COMMITTED transactions, calls verify/1 before serving, registers one config per queue, keeps the prefix, search binding, embedding binding, provider account and request of a config while any of its ingests is not terminal, sets Oban Lifeline rescue_after above the largest step deadline plus 60 s, and uses a durable intent Store for the no-send classification.

telemetry.contract: Oban [:oban, :job, ...] and Ecto query events of the consumer's Oban instance and Repo; the Piece emits no Elzoo event and its queries pass log: false.

config.contract: Construction-time only (new/1, fixed for the value's life): repo, prefix, oban, queue (1..64 bytes), search, artifact, artifact_scopes (0..16), embedding (max_input_bytes at least 8,000), request (model and dimension of the index descriptor), intent and max_attempts 1..5 (default 3); per-request chunking chunk_size 2,000..8,192, chunk_overlap 0..200, max_chunks 1..65,536; fixed version 1 step deadlines 120,000 ms, receive_timeout_ms + 30,000 ms and 120,000 ms.

control.contract: cancel/3 and resubmit/3 per ingest; Oban queue pause and resume are inherited from the consumer's Oban instance.
